primitives.name: Streaming latency model
primitives.assumptions: (1) Network bitrate R follows a stationary stochastic process; (2) Buffer size B is finite and constant; (3) Streaming client operates under a "buffer-full" policy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: L → ∞ when R drops below a critical threshold R_c = B / C, causing infinite rebuffering.

layer2.mapping: Maps to NFL's adaptive bitrate streaming control as a conformal prediction interval for future bitrate.
layer2.telemetry: Observed rebuffering events per stream segment serve as empirical calibration statistics.

primitives.name: Demdex identifier resolution
primitives.assumptions: (1) User sessions follow a renewal process; (2) Feature vectors F are drawn i.i.d. from a fixed distribution; (3) Persistence probability P depends only on the last observed feature.
primitives.breakdown_regime: V becomes non-unique when two distinct user trajectories produce identical F sequences, leading to identity collision.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI sequential decision trees for bettor clustering via behavioral features.
layer2.telemetry: Identity collision frequency serves as a leakage indicator for information asymmetry in betting pools.

primitives.name: Cookie consent optimization
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'Consent utility (dollars)', 'O': 'Opt-in rate (dimensionless)', 'P': 'Privacy cost (dollars per bit of data)', 'U': 'User surplus (dollars)', 'M': 'Marketing revenue (dollars)'}
primitives.assumptions: (1) User opt-in decisions maximize expected utility E[U - P]; (2) Marketing revenue M scales linearly with O; (3) Privacy costs P are convex in data exposure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: O → 0 as P exceeds a regulatory threshold P_r, causing consent system to collapse into pure anonymization.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian optimal mechanism design for maximizing platform revenue subject to GDPR constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Revenue loss due to consent opt-outs provides empirical feedback for dynamic pricing of user data.

primitives.name: Ping latency probe
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D': 'Round-trip delay (seconds)', 'Q': 'Packet queue length (packets)', 'L': 'Link capacity (bps)', 'M': 'Maximum transmission unit (bytes)'}
primitives.assumptions: (1) Network traffic follows an M/M/1 queue; (2) Propagation delay is negligible compared to queuing delay; (3) Packet loss probability is constant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: D → ∞ when link utilization ρ approaches 1, indicating network congestion.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state-transition model for predicting game-time network failures affecting live-stream quality.
layer2.telemetry: Historical D distributions inform Markov decision processes for switching between streaming resolutions.
